author: Torta
subject: Level One Lunatic
content_md:
****What is the Level One Lunatic challenge?****

During this challenge, you'll push the limits of a level **one** character and earn exclusive titles to prove just how far a noob can go:

- ****The Wee Warlord**** — earn **10,000 honorable kills** to show you're more than just fresh meat.

- ****Pint-Sized Politician**** — reach **Exalted** with at least one faction to prove that even a tiny hero can have powerful friends.

- ****Arena’s Smallest Smasher**** — obtain the **Arena Master Trinket** to demonstrate that, even at level one, you’re an unstoppable force of nature.

- ****Hero of Goldshire**** (Alliance) / ****Lazy Peon's Foreman**** (Horde) — complete **100 quests** available to you, earning the respect of tutorial NPCs everywhere.

![level_one_lunatic-CXjIpv52.png](./download/file.php?id=125) <dd>level_one_lunatic-CXjIpv52.png (761.2 KiB) Viewed 96746 times</dd>

 ****How to begin the challenge?****

Simply speak to any Glyph Scribe at any starting location to sign up!

---
 ****How do Lunatics communicate?****

By default, new characters on Turtle WoW cannot speak until they reach level 5 to prevent spam bots. However, Lunatics who complete **30 quests** at level 1 and spend **at least 10 hours in-game** will unlock chat privileges! You can also join the ****/lunatic**** channel in-game. This is a community chat.

---
 ****Are battlegrounds & arenas available at level 1?****

Yes! The ****Warsong Gulch 1-9 bracket**** and ****Blood Ring**** are available to all levels.

Since **Turtle WoW** was the first realm to introduce this challenge, we're celebrating with a special **wallpaper** made by our talented artist **Lionell Schramm**!

![level_one_lunatic(1).jpg](./download/file.php?id=126) <dd>level_one_lunatic(1).jpg (833.49 KiB) Viewed 96746 times</dd>

Full Size: <https://turtlecraft.gg/images/level_one_lunatic.jpg>

Stay tuned, keep fighting, and remember size doesn't matter when you have determination and possibly a really sharp dagger.

author: StabsMcKenzy
subject: Re: Level One Lunatic Info & Rankings
content_md:
> **Xudo wrote: Thu Feb 20, 2025 4:30 pm**
> While I don't really like idea of lvl 1 lunatics, I am still impressed by twow devs work regarding that challenge.
>
>  Though, I am curious, did merging 1-1 and 2-9 brackets actually increased amount of battlegrounds for people?
>  584 characters on 6k realm doesn't look very impressive tbh. I still insist that high level enchants should be nerfed.

If you think about the actuality of wpvp on Nord, the lunatic challenge is absolutely a net positive.

Would you rather lvl 60s ganking sub lvl 20s or lvl 1 twinks ganking sub lvl 20s? The answer is easy and obvious, the lvl 1s. The lvl 1 gankers provide something lvl 60 gankers don't , a sense of hope and possibility TM. The amount of options players have for dealing with a lvl 1 twink is drastically higher than for a lvl 60.

It would take an army of lvl 1s to kill a lvl 1 twink without coordination but if 3 lvl 1 mages knew how to pvp they could absolutely lock a lvl 1 down to death with just frost bolts and kiting. You can really mix that combo up however you like and even just have a few decently coordinated lvl 5 randos and they too can kill the lvl 1. What this challenge does is highlight the power of teamwork in pvp, and it does it in a way that provides clear boundries and options. If a lvl 1 can't beat the twink, then they ask someone for help, be it another lvl 1 or even a lvl 60. If that lvl 60 shows up, the twink is toast (or has to play cat and mouse, either way that twink ain't killing the 60), if a second lvl 1 shows up, those two stand a much higher chance of winning if they work together. If those two lvl 1s fail then they can call in another, that process repeats until they win. When that group of lvl 1s finally kills that twink they feel like they've taken down a raid boss and they haven't even left the starting zone, or the group is thankful to a lvl 60 for the protection, either way social interactions have been had and nothing unites players like having a shared enemy. It's also worth noting that if at any point they want to give up and not pvp they can, pvp is entirely opt in.

The lvl 1 gankers provide something lvl 60 gankers don't , a sense of hope and possibility TM. The amount of options players have for dealing with a lvl 1 twink is drastically higher than for a lvl 60.

It would take an army of lvl 1s to kill a lvl 1 twink without coordination but if 3 lvl 1 mages knew how to pvp they could absolutely lock a lvl 1 down to death with just frost bolts and kiting. You can really mix that combo up however you like and even just have a few decently coordinated lvl 5 randos and they too can kill the lvl 1. What this challenge does is highlight the power of teamwork in pvp, and it does it in a way that provides clear boundries and options. If a lvl 1 can't beat the twink, then they ask someone for help, be it another lvl 1 or even a lvl 60. If that lvl 60 shows up, the twink is toast (or has to play cat and mouse, either way that twink ain't killing the 60), if a second lvl 1 shows up, those two stand a much higher chance of winning if they work together. If those two lvl 1s fail then they can call in another, that process repeats until they win. When that group of lvl 1s finally kills that twink they feel like they've taken down a raid boss and they haven't even left the starting zone, or the group is thankful to a lvl 60 for the protection, either way social interactions have been had and nothing unites players like having a shared enemy. It's also worth noting that if at any point they want to give up and not pvp they can, pvp is entirely opt in.

To be honest, I understand reasoning behind that requirement. This number of HK is supposed to bind character to that level and location for long time. Challenge was designed in a way that normal players become "boss"-like enemies. With tons of hp and damage, so you have to gather a party to kill one.
This particular goal was achieved successfully. Now there are 600 little bosses all around the world. I hope people have enough fun with that.
I had very similar suggestion year ago [Troublemaker achievement for PvP realm](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=11996). I just didn't intent to bind players to specific level forever.

 100 quests as lvl 1 sounds like "make all quests, then buy race change, then make all quests for opposite side" or like "participate in every holiday event during all year". Lunar festival with blessing features like 50 quests for lvl 1. All quests in starting zones are probably ~20 in total. DMF has ~10 quest.

author: Xudo
subject: Re: Level One Lunatic Info & Rankings
content_md:
I am not sure that 9 level has perfect pvp balance too. So I'd expand possible skills to lvl 19.

I'd add Overpower to warriors. It is lvl 12 spell, but as long as dodge is important, I think it is fair to add skill to counter it. Alternatively, I'd add Hamstring. It won't be very powerful, because everyone will stack on dodge.
But basic toolkit of warriors is miserable. All you have is autoattack and a bit stronger autoattack. By default you can't kill any class with heal button. I tried. Mana of casters regenerates very quickly while your health don't regenerates at all.

For hunters I'd add Track Humanoids and Hunter's Mark. Reconnaissance is their key feature. Hunters already got their instant attack as Raptor Strike from CC2, so they are pretty fine.

I think only 1 ranged CC ability should be added for mages. Even if their frost armor is defensive, it still helps to kite.
From your options, after some thoughts, I would pick Sheep. Because it is not spammable no-brainer skill. You can use it only once and it have drawback in a form of enemy life regeneration.

Those additional skills can be granted by completing additional class quests. For example warlock get imp from lvl 4 quest. Characters with natural progression will get those abilities later, but Lunatics can bother doing overleveled quests.

content_md:
I put a lot of thought into my list of abilities and I disagree with Hamstring and Concussive Shot. We have access to Goblin Rocket Boots and PVP Trinket so adding too many slows would be bad. It fits what they are trying to do and even still they might get run down with Rocket Boots, PVP Trinket, or Discombobulator Ray. I fully expect the Warrior to still lose that encounter but atleast feeling like it's possible with Thunderclap and getting lucky hitting them from behind a few times. Overpower would be too strong and it would be up at all times and even if they considered it they would have to make a even lower level version of it, that's asking a lot and I don't think it would be fair. Keep abilities in the same bracket.

content_html:
What is the Level One Lunatic challenge?

During this challenge, you'll push the limits of a level one character and earn exclusive titles to prove just how far a noob can go:
  • The Wee Warlord — earn 10,000 honorable kills to show you're more than just fresh meat.
  • Pint-Sized Politician — reach Exalted with at least one faction to prove that even a tiny hero can have powerful friends.
  • Arena’s Smallest Smasher — obtain the Arena Master Trinket to demonstrate that, even at level one, you’re an unstoppable force of nature.
  • Hero of Goldshire (Alliance) / Lazy Peon's Foreman (Horde) — complete 100 quests available to you, earning the respect of tutorial NPCs everywhere.


level_one_lunatic-CXjIpv52.png



How to begin the challenge?

Simply speak to any Glyph Scribe at any starting location to sign up!

How do Lunatics communicate?

By default, new characters on Turtle WoW cannot speak until they reach level 5 to prevent spam bots. However, Lunatics who complete 30 quests at level 1 and spend at least 10 hours in-game will unlock chat privileges! You can also join the /lunatic channel in-game. This is a community chat.

Are battlegrounds & arenas available at level 1?

Yes! The Warsong Gulch 1-9 bracket and Blood Ring are available to all levels.


Since Turtle WoW was the first realm to introduce this challenge, we're celebrating with a special wallpaper made by our talented artist Lionell Schramm!


level_one_lunatic(1).jpg


Full Size: https://turtlecraft.gg/images/level_one_lunatic.jpg

Stay tuned, keep fighting, and remember size doesn't matter when you have determination and possibly a really sharp dagger.
Could use an update for the Exploration Title.

Also I was curious if there is any consideration on reducing the level requirement of this Quest to Level 1.

https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?quest=60030

Fashion Coins are nearly impossible to get and are widely available to everyone else on the server.

Thank you Torta.

subject: Cysthetic's Lunatic Paladin Guide
content_md:
Welcome to my
⁺  . ✦ Lunatic Paladin Guide ✦ . ⁺
 *Where you learn that Rogue may perhaps not be the only good class in this Bracket.*

Lets get things started.

 **Before you read anything else you need the following Addon.**

 **ItemRack**
 *<https://turtle-wow.fandom.com/wiki/ItemRack>*

 **Quickheal**
 *<https://github.com/Zebouski/QuickHeal>*

Note: In regards to Quickheal I am aware many people dislike automation addons. The reason for its inclusion is our Heal is tied to a Weapon Swap Macro. I typically use an Alt Selfcast Addon but it doesn't work with macro'd Heals. This is the best way I have found for now, I'll update it with a change in the future if I can find out other methods.

 **Spells**

 **Devotion Aura**
Gives 55 additional armor to party members. 30 Yard Range.
 **Note: Armor Scaling is very good at Level 1.**

 **Seal of Righteousness**
 20 Mana
Hits for 1-2 with a 1H Equipped and 3-4 with a 2H Equipped.
This has a chance to trigger Weapon Enchants.
In PVE this can also trigger on attacks that Miss.
For full DPS Builds and PVE I recommend using a 2h for higher Proc Rates.
Recommend putting Fiery on a Mutton Chop and making an ItemRack load out called (FIRE) to equip it.

These are the following Macros I use:
/script EquipSet("FIRE")
/cast Seal of Righteousness(Rank 1)

/script EquipSet("FIRE")
(Sometimes it's not worth the Mana to Cast Seal).

 **Holy Light**
 35 Mana
This Heals for 39-48 with a 2.5 Second Cast. 40 Yard Range.
This has 33% Scaling with +Healing.
.25 Threat Modifier in PVE.
Recommend putting +55 Healing on a Mutton Chop and making an ItemRack load out called (HEALS) to equip it.

These are the following Macros I use:
The Importance of these Macros is to Swap from Fiery to Healing without the Global in Combat and Heal Instantly.

 **With Target:**
/script EquipSet("HEALS")
/cast Holy Light(Rank 1)

 **Targeting Self:**
/target character name
/script EquipSet("HEALS")
/cast Holy Light(Rank 1)

 **Target Lowest Health Target:**
/script EquipSet("HEALS")
/quickheal

 *As well as additional Macros for DPS Sets, Intellect Weapon, Spirit Weapon/Spirit Shield.*

 **MATH**
Holy Light +55 Healing Weapon: 57-66.
Holy Light +55 Healing Weapon, +30 Healing Gloves: 67-76.
Holy Light +55 Healing Weapon, +30 Healing Gloves, +24 Healing Bracers: 75-84.
Holy Light +55 Healing Weapon, +30 Healing Gloves, +24 Healing Bracers, +31 Healing Shoulders: 85-94.

 **SIMPLER MATH**
Holy Light +55 Healing to Weapon: Adds 18 Healing.
Holy Light +30 Healing to Gloves: Adds 10 Healing.
Holy Light +24 Healing to Bracers: Adds 8 Healing.
Holy Light +31 Healing to Shoulders: Adds 10 Healing.
Holy Light +12 Healing to Head or Legs: Adds 4 Healing.

 **Recommended Race: Human**

 **The Human Spirit**
Increases Spirit by 5%, and allows 5% of your Mana Regeneration to continue while casting.
Note: This Regeneration is noticeable as it is 2 mana every few seconds with All Stat Enchants.
 **Note: Mana Regenerates very quickly at Level 1.**

 **Perception**
Increases Stealth Detection and grants 2% spell and physical critical strike chance.
Lasts 20 Seconds.

 **Diplomacy**
Increases Reputation Gain by 10%

 **Professions**

 **First Aid**
 225 Skill Obtainable.

 **Herbalism**
 75 Skill Obtainable.

 **Mining**
 75 Skill Obtainable.

 **Consumables**

 **Minor Healing Potion**
Use: Restores 70 to 91 health.
 2 Minute Cooldown.

 **Scroll of Protection**
Increases Armor by 60.
Lasts 30 Minutes.

 **Scroll of Spirit**
Increases Spirit by 3.
Lasts 30 Minutes.

 **Rumsey Rum Black Label**
Increases Stamina by 15.
Lasts 15 Minutes.

 **Watered-down Beer**
Reduces Stamina by 1, Increases Spirit by 1.
(This is a debuff that stacks with Rumsey).

 **Fizzy Energy Drink**
Well Fed: 6 Mana per 5.
Lasts 15 Minutes.

 **Weak Troll's Blood Potion**
Regenerates 2 health every 5 seconds.
Lasts 1 Hour.

 **Elixir of Lion's Strength**
Increases Strength by 4.
Lasts 1 Hour.

 **Elixir of Minor Defense**
Increases armor by 50.
Lasts 1 Hour.
(Does not stack with Scroll of Protection).

 **Discombobulator Ray**
Use: Transforms the target into a Leper Gnome, reducing its melee and spell damage by 40 and its movement rate by 20% for 12 sec.
 1 Minute Cooldown, 20 Yard Range.

 **Heavy Runecloth Bandage**
Use: Heals 2000 damage over 8 Seconds.
(Requires 225 First Aid).

 **World Buffs**

 **Darkmoon Faire Buff from Sayge**
 10% Stamina Combination: Confiscate the Corn, Speak against your brother openly. (3,1).
 10% Armor Combination : Slay the man, Let your friend go. (1, 3).
 10% Damage Combination: Slay the man, Execute your friend painfully. (1,1).
 10% Intellect Combination: Turn him over to liege, Show not so quiet defiance. (2,2).
 25 All Resist Combination: Turn him over to liege, Remain Quiet. (2,3).

ItemRack

Quickheal
https://github.com/Zebouski/QuickHeal

Devotion Aura
Gives 55 additional armor to party members. 30 Yard Range.
Note: Armor Scaling is very good at Level 1.

Seal of Righteousness
20 Mana
Hits for 1-2 with a 1H Equipped and 3-4 with a 2H Equipped.
This has a chance to trigger Weapon Enchants.
In PVE this can also trigger on attacks that Miss.
For full DPS Builds and PVE I recommend using a 2h for higher Proc Rates.
Recommend putting Fiery on a Mutton Chop and making an ItemRack load out called (FIRE) to equip it.

These are the following Macros I use:
/script EquipSet("FIRE")
/cast Seal of Righteousness(Rank 1)

/script EquipSet("FIRE")
(Sometimes it's not worth the Mana to Cast Seal).

Holy Light
35 Mana
This Heals for 39-48 with a 2.5 Second Cast. 40 Yard Range.
This has 33% Scaling with +Healing.
.25 Threat Modifier in PVE.
Recommend putting +55 Healing on a Mutton Chop and making an ItemRack load out called (HEALS) to equip it.

These are the following Macros I use:
The Importance of these Macros is to Swap from Fiery to Healing without the Global in Combat and Heal Instantly.

With Target:
/script EquipSet("HEALS")
/cast Holy Light(Rank 1)

Targeting Self:
/target character name
/script EquipSet("HEALS")
/cast Holy Light(Rank 1)

Target Lowest Health Target:
/script EquipSet("HEALS")
/quickheal

author: KemperGuy
subject: Lunatic on PvP server = near impossible
content_md:
So it just dawned on me - it's actually near impossible to do the lunatic on a PvP server (ironically).

Why? Because you can't enable warmode on a PvP server - which means players in starting zones aren't enabled for PvP.

Anyone entering a contested zone is already 10+ and near impossible to kill.

The only option would be battlegrounds, but I've been in a queue for one for 10 hours now and still nothing, so yeah. I love a challenge, but without anyone under level 10 to do PvP against... what is one supposed to do?

author: StabsMcKenzy
subject: Lunatic Guild <Level One Lunatic>
content_md:
Welcome to <Level One Lunatic> on Nordanaar
A Turtle WoW PvP Guild unlike any other!

We embrace the chaos of playing at Level 1 and the thrill of ganking players while we push ourselves to achieve some of the most challenging and unique goals in the game.

Whether it’s reaching Exalted with reputations, completing 100 quests, obtaining the Arena Grand Master, or pushing to an impressive 10,000 kills, we take pride in pushing the boundaries of what’s possible for Level 1 characters.

We are fully dedicated to growing this community. We provide a Minor Speed Enchant for Boots to new members and hope to revive this bracket, encouraging more active participation in Battlegrounds.

Our guild is built on the spirit of fun and while we dive into these challenging feats, we are committed to fostering a friendly, respectful environment where every guild member feels supported. Harassment and toxicity have no place here.

As we tackle these insane challenges, we do it with a sense of humor and an understanding that the journey is just as important as the destination.

Being a Level One Lunatic is all about teamwork and helping each other rise to the occasion. Whether you're working toward any of these challenges or you need support in a tough fight, you’ll find a community here that’s always ready to lend a hand.

The beauty of our guild is that, despite our unusual starting point, we are all in this together. Your success is our success, and we’re always eager to help each other along the way.

If you're looking for a guild where you can share in the thrill of ganking and grinding, taking on ambitious goals, and making lasting memories with a group of like-minded lunatics, then you've come to the right place.

Take your experience on Turtle WoW to a whole new level ~ literally.

Reach out to Stabsmckenzy or Cysthen for a guild invite!

Friendly reminder to please be familiar with the Rules.
Dualboxing in PVP flagged environments is strictly prohibited.
<https://turtlecraft.gg/rules>

author: Nemetth1
subject: Level One Lunatic: A Complete Misunderstanding of What PvP Is
content_md:
Good afternoon, community. I’d like to bring up a topic that I believe is significant and still can’t quite understand—specifically, the reasoning behind implementing such a challenge/objective that creates an undesirable environment for the vast majority of players while providing questionable enjoyment for a small minority.

While I find the Level One Lunatic challenge interesting in contexts like Battlegrounds or real PvP—where there’s a fair balance of power between opponents—I can’t wrap my head around the idea that the GMs’ true intention is to foster the current scenario.

> **Sleeptime wrote: Mon Apr 28, 2025 10:17 pm**
> Hey there!
>
>  Spawn camping and corpse camping are allowed, as PvP is optional and players can choose to opt out. This isn’t considered griefing or anything like that. You’re free to camp starting zones all day long if you want to.

In other words: I cannot comprehend, from any possible angle, how having a level 1 character with level 60 enchants endlessly killing freshly created characters—while using "PvP is optional" as a valid excuse from the server’s leadership—is acceptable.

I believe this stems from a fundamental misunderstanding of what PvP is and isn’t. A character one-shotting others isn’t PvP—it’s systematized bullying. For PvP to exist, there MUST be at least some semblance of a fair fight between opponents. It’s the same distinction we’d make in the real world between war and invasion. If the victim has no means to defend themselves, it’s not PvP—it’s simply bullying.

Some might argue: "Well, if a level 60 character kills you while you’re leveling, it’s the same thing." But no, it’s not the same. While my previous argument might seem to apply here as well, allow me to highlight a subtle difference. In that scenario, the player has options: rezzing stealthily and using Hearthstone, rezzing at the angel, or even asking a Warlock for a summon. But for a freshly created level 1 character, none of these options exist when they’re systematically ganked just meters from their spawn point.

My proposal: Remove this dynamic. It’s not fun. It’s not okay. It encourages a despicable social behavior. Implement a restriction preventing attacks on characters below level 5. This would protect genuinely new players while preserving free PvP for those who already have basic tools.

Regards!

This isn’t a rage post: I haven’t created level 1 characters in a long time, but I constantly hear complaints from new players trying to start and encountering this situation.

Howdy there, Nem! This is a well written post. I believe I can provide some clarity for you though.

"creates an undesirable environment for the vast majority of players while providing questionable enjoyment for a small minority."

In my experience this isn't the case at all. Most people simply don't interact with the pvp on Turtle wow. And the Lunatics who do the challenge generally have a lot of fun with it.

"While I find the Level One Lunatic challenge interesting in contexts like Battlegrounds or real PvP—where there’s a fair balance of power between opponents—I can’t wrap my head around the idea that the GMs’ true intention is to foster the current scenario."

What's the difference between a lvl 1 with no gear queuing for a bg and a lvl 1 with no gear opting in for pvp? Surely you're not saying that a no gear lvl 1 stands a chance against a lvl 1 twink. Personally, as long as everyone is consenting I don't think there's an issue, if a no gear lvl 1 wants to bg, who am I to them they can't?

"I believe this stems from a fundamental misunderstanding of what PvP is and isn’t. A character one-shotting others isn’t PvP—it’s systematized bullying. For PvP to exist, there MUST be at least some semblance of a fair fight between opponents. It’s the same distinction we’d make in the real world between war and invasion. If the victim has no means to defend themselves, it’s not PvP—it’s simply bullying."

This is probably the biggest point. You believe that if a fight is unfair, that it's not pvp. You'd, technically, be incorrect. PvP directly stands for player vs player, not player vs player but with fairness. The closest thing to what you're speaking about is called Competitive PvP, and that's where balance and fairness come into play. There's a common misconception that vanilla wow had competitive pvp, it doesn't though. Competitive pvp wasn't introduced until Burning Crusade through the Arena System.

"Some might argue: "Well, if a level 60 character kills you while you’re leveling, it’s the same thing." But no, it’s not the same. While my previous argument might seem to apply here as well, allow me to highlight a subtle difference. In that scenario, the player has options: rezzing stealthily and using Hearthstone, rezzing at the angel, or even asking a Warlock for a summon. But for a freshly created level 1 character, none of these options exist when they’re systematically ganked just meters from their spawn point."

Those players can simply deflag or in the case of warmoders they can corpse hop over to a battlemaster to deactivate warmode, or simply go to another area to level. There's always options, and opting out of pvp is a valid one. To your point though, this challenge is different on a pvp server because of how flagging works so Tel'abim is always an option for players who want a slightly more balanced approach to lvl 1 anti-ganking.

"My proposal: Remove this dynamic. It’s not fun. It’s not okay. It encourages a despicable social behavior. Implement a restriction preventing attacks on characters below level 5. This would protect genuinely new players while preserving free PvP for those who already have basic tools."

Not that I have any say but I certainly hope they don't remove it. It is fun, it is okay as it's all consensual. It doesn't encourage despicable social behavior, there's no advantage given to players who are rude or break rules. Tel'abim has the resrictions you speak of, in a way, so you could try playing there. New players are already protected on Nord as they have to opt in to pvp.

While I'm sure the complaints are annoying, the solution is incredibly simple and widely available so you have to wonder how justified those complaints really are.

Personally, as long as everyone is consenting I don't think there's an issue, if a no gear lvl 1 wants to bg, who am I to them they can't?


"I believe this stems from a fundamental misunderstanding of what PvP is and isn’t. A character one-shotting others isn’t PvP—it’s systematized bullying. For PvP to exist, there MUST be at least some semblance of a fair fight between opponents. It’s the same distinction we’d make in the real world between war and invasion. If the victim has no means to defend themselves, it’s not PvP—it’s simply bullying."

This is probably the biggest point. You believe that if a fight is unfair, that it's not pvp. You'd, technically, be incorrect. PvP directly stands for player vs player, not player vs player but with fairness. The closest thing to what you're speaking about is called Competitive PvP, and that's where balance and fairness come into play. There's a common misconception that vanilla wow had competitive pvp, it doesn't though. Competitive pvp wasn't introduced until Burning Crusade through the Arena System.


"Some might argue: "Well, if a level 60 character kills you while you’re leveling, it’s the same thing." But no, it’s not the same. While my previous argument might seem to apply here as well, allow me to highlight a subtle difference. In that scenario, the player has options: rezzing stealthily and using Hearthstone, rezzing at the angel, or even asking a Warlock for a summon. But for a freshly created level 1 character, none of these options exist when they’re systematically ganked just meters from their spawn point."

Those players can simply deflag or in the case of warmoders they can corpse hop over to a battlemaster to deactivate warmode, or simply go to another area to level. There's always options, and opting out of pvp is a valid one. To your point though, this challenge is different on a pvp server because of how flagging works so Tel'abim is always an option for players who want a slightly more balanced approach to lvl 1 anti-ganking.


"My proposal: Remove this dynamic. It’s not fun. It’s not okay. It encourages a despicable social behavior. Implement a restriction preventing attacks on characters below level 5. This would protect genuinely new players while preserving free PvP for those who already have basic tools."

Not that I have any say but I certainly hope they don't remove it. It is fun, it is okay as it's all consensual. It doesn't encourage despicable social behavior, there's no advantage given to players who are rude or break rules. Tel'abim has the resrictions you speak of, in a way, so you could try playing there. New players are already protected on Nord as they have to opt in to pvp.


While I'm sure the complaints are annoying, the solution is incredibly simple and widely available so you have to wonder how justified those complaints really are.

author: StabsMcKenzy
subject: Level One Lunatic Guide
content_md:
LEVEL ONE LUNATIC GUIDE (not updated for RFC or DM)

The Level One Lunatic Challenge
Simply put, this server challenge requires you to perform challenges at level 1 that would normally not be done until a much higher level. There are 4 sub-challenges, each reward a title that you can keep even if you level up. These are the Titles, and the requirements:
Wee Warlord - requires the player to get 10,000 honorable kills
Pint-Sized Politician - requires the player to reach exalted with any faction
Arena's Smallest Smasher - requires the player to obtain Arena Grand Master
Hero of Goldshire/Lazy Peon's Foreman - requires the player complete 100 quests

The Official Forum post for the challenge: [Level One Lunatic Info & Rankings](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=17653)

Starting The Challenge
In each of the starting zones there is a "Glyph Master", at the glyph master you'll purchase "Glyph of the Wee Warlord", you must be level 1 in order to take the challenge and doing so will turn off your ability to gain xp. I would recommend you not take any of the other challenges while doing this one.

Removing Chat Restrictions
Level 1 characters are unable to use /say, /yell, /world, and /whisper,  you can still invite people to party and speak with them there. This restriction can be removed by completing 30 quests and spending 10 hours in game. Doing the quests in all of your faction's starting zones will get you more than the 30 quests required. Joining a guild will also allow you to speak in guild chat.

Lunatic Guilds
There's a handful of guilds that will assist Lunatics in their goals:
<Level One Lunatic> is specifically designed for helping Lunatics. Their guild teleport is in booty Bay for easy access to Gurubashi Arena.
<Macrochelys> is helpful towards Lunatics and offers a high quality raiding scene should you choose to level up after finishing the challenge. Their guild teleport is to Azshara and comes with a gryphon to ride to Durotar.

There's also a few guilds with guild bases that don't tolerate Lunatics, so you'll have to get creative to get into them:
<The Scourge> - Tirisfal Glades
<The Scarlett Crusade> - Tirisfal Glades
<The Blackwing Guard> - Elwynn Forest (via Burning Steppes)
<The Lion's Pride Legion> - Elwynn Forest (via Duskwood)

The Setup
Mods used:
 1. SuperWow
This mod is required to use ShaguScan, you'll also use it to launch wow.
 2. VanillaTweaks
You'll use this mod to set your name plate view distance to 99.
 3. ShaguScan
This mod allows you to make a list of available pvp targets near you. The scan parameters I use are(it should be copy-pastable for the mod filter line):
player,alliance,pvp,alive,attack
This makes it so that all living flagged alliance show up on a list, you'll change alliance to horde if you're playing an alliance. This should make hunting players less visually intensive.
 4. ShaguPlates
Use this to customize nameplates so that health bars only show up for the unit you're targetting, and make the targetted hp bar easier to see. the options you're looking for are "Always Show On Target Units" and "Hide Healthbar On enemynpc/enemyplayer/neutralnpc" This way when you have nameplates on and you target a player on your ShaguScan list you're able to scan visually for them MUCH easier thanks to the VanillaTweaks nameplate distance increase.

Character:
Class:

Rogue - This is the class to pick for this challenge, they fit the bill in every way. Sinister Strike and Eviscerate provide ample damage on their own, plus they proc fiery. They scale VERY well on agility, even reaching above 100% dodge. The cherry on top is they have access to stealth at level 1.

Paladin – Can heal and tank well. Gear should be a mix of healing power, stamina, and armor. Weapon should be a Half-eaten Mutton Chop with fiery and +55 healing.
[Cysthen's Paladin Guide](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=17957)

Warrior – Does good damage and can tank well. Gear should be enchanted with a lot of stamina and some strength. Weapons should have fiery, crusader, and lifesteal. Troll warriors can be scaled heavily with spirit to produce very high in combat regen.

Hunter – Does good damage, expensive to use because of twink ammo. Gear should be primarily agility, with some stamina. Weapons should have +25agi and fiery.

Shaman – Does good damage and some light tanking. Gear should be mostly stamina with some strength. Weapon should be a Half-eaten Mutton Chop with fiery.

Mage, Priest, Warlock, Druid – Able to do the challenge but are working entirely off stats instead of kit. Gear is entirely stamina. Weapon should be a Half-eaten Mutton Chop with fiery.

The tier order I believe I'd put the classes in is as follows: Rogue > Paladin > Warrior = Hunter > Shaman > Mage > Priest = Warlock = Druid

Race:
Goblin - Gives you +3 to dagger skill, and a 40% for 5s sprint on a 3min cd.
Night Elf - Gives you 1% increase to atk spd, casting spd, move spd, and dodge chance. You move 50% faster while dead, which is often. And you get access to shadowmeld which is an unmoving stealth on a 1min cd then doesn't break for 2 seconds after moving, or better stealth level if rogue. This race makes playing Warrior, Hunter, Priest, or Druid more viable then their non-NE counterparts.
Gnome - Gets 10 arcane resist which helps vs polymorph, and Escape Artist which removes and immobilization or movement speed reducing effect, on a 1.5min cd

Gear:
 1. Helm
There's a few things you can get here like:
[Woolen Cowl](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=51219) (lvl 6 ally quest reward)
[Red Defias Mask](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=7997) (mob drop near deadmines)
[Scruffy Cloth Hat](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=70032) (lvl 7 horde quest)
OR IF YOU BIG BALLIN'
[Queen Azshara's Crown](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=81304) (Buy from Zeet Waxwrench in Sparkwater Port for 1k g) - 51 armor
Enchant - +8 Agi (Libram of Voracity, requires a lvl 50 to finish quest and apply the enchant)

 2. Necklace
[Voice Amplification Modulator](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=16009) (made by engineer)
Enchant - +6 Agi (Gemology Jewelcrafting 225)

 3. Shoulders
Blackened Leather Spaulders (drops from Gregor Agamand) - BoP with 29 armor
Enchant - +16 stam and +100 armor
Gregor Agamand is a named mob located in northern Agamand Mills in northern Tirisfal Glades

 4. Cape
[Linen Cloak](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=2570) (made by a tailor) - 6 armor
Enchant - +3 Agi (Enchanting 225)

 5. Chest
[Dirty Leather Vest](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=85) (Buy from starting zone leather vendor) - 33 armor
Enchant - +4 All Stats (Enchanting 300)

 6. Wrist
[Dirty Leather Bracers](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=1836) (Buy from starting zone leather vendor) - 15 armor
Enchant - +7 Agi (Enchanting 300)

 7. Gloves
[Dirty Leather Gloves](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=714) (Buy from starting zone leather vendor) - 21 armor
Enchants - +15 Agi (Enchanting 300)

 8. Waist
[Squealer's Belt](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=4951) (Drops from "Squealer" Thornmantle) - 23 armor
Enchant - +6 Agi (190 Blacksmithing)
"Squealer" Thornmantle can be found in a cave located near the quillboard chieftan's hut in Brambleblade Ravine located in southern Mulgore, within the starting zone

 9. Legs
[Dirty Leather Pants](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=209) (Buy from starting zone leather vendor) - 29 armor
Enchant - +8 Agi (Libram of Voracity, requires a lvl 50 to finish quest and apply the enchant)

 10. Boots
[Goblin Rocket Boots](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=7189) (made by engineer) - 41 armor, Use Effect: 70% increased move speed for 20 seconds, chance to break on use.
Enchant - Minor Speed (Enchanting 225)

 11. Rings
[Silver Piffeny Ring](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=7342) (buy from Qixdi Goodstitch for 10g in Booty Bay)
Enchant - +6 Agi (Gemology Jewelcrafting 225)
You're going to want two of these rings

 12. Trinkets
[Insignia of the Horde](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=18849)/Alliance (Purchase from pvp vendor in capital after reaching Honor rank 2) - Use Effect: Dispels all types of crowd control effects
[Arena Grand Master](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=19024) (Obtained from Gurubashi Arena chest quest) - 1% dodge, Use Effect: Absorbs 750 to 1250 damage and lasts 20 seconds

 13. Weapons
[Simple Dagger](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=4565) (Drops from any starter zone mobs) - 3-6 dmg, 1.8 atk spd
Enchant - +15 Agi (Enchanting 300) And/Or Fiery (Enchanting 265)

[Furbolg Medicine Pouch](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=16768) (Buy from Timbermaw Hold after reaching Honored) - +10 Stam, Use Effect: Restores 100 health every second for 10 seconds on a 20minute CD

[Cadet's Bow](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=8179) (Drops from any starter zone mobs) - 3-6 dmg, 2.0 atk spd
Scope - +7 dmg (Engineering 240)
[Feathered Arrow](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=3464) (Quest reward from "Stolen Supplies" a Gelkis quest in Desolace) - 9.5 dmg

 14. Consumables
[Heavy Runecloth Bandage](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=14530) (Requires 290 First Aid to make)  - Use Effect: Heals 2000 damage over 8 seconds (Requires 225 First Aid to use)
[Minor Healing Potions](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=118) - Use Effect: Restores 70 to 90 health
[Discombobulator Ray](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=4388) (Engineering 160 to make) - Use Effect: Transforms the target into a leper gnome, reducing its melee and spell damage by 40 and it's movement rate by 20% for 12 seconds on a 1minute cd
[Rumsey Rum Light/Dark/Black Label](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?search=Rumsey+Rum) - Use Effect: Increases staming by 5/10/15 for 15minutes

LEVEL ONE LUNATIC GUIDE (not updated for RFC or DM)

The Level One Lunatic Challenge
Simply put, this server challenge requires you to perform challenges at level 1 that would normally not be done until a much higher level. There are 4 sub-challenges, each reward a title that you can keep even if you level up. These are the Titles, and the requirements:
Wee Warlord - requires the player to get 10,000 honorable kills
Pint-Sized Politician - requires the player to reach exalted with any faction
Arena's Smallest Smasher - requires the player to obtain Arena Grand Master
Hero of Goldshire/Lazy Peon's Foreman - requires the player complete 100 quests

The Official Forum post for the challenge: Level One Lunatic Info & Rankings

Starting The Challenge
In each of the starting zones there is a "Glyph Master", at the glyph master you'll purchase "Glyph of the Wee Warlord", you must be level 1 in order to take the challenge and doing so will turn off your ability to gain xp. I would recommend you not take any of the other challenges while doing this one.

Removing Chat Restrictions
Level 1 characters are unable to use /say, /yell, /world, and /whisper, you can still invite people to party and speak with them there. This restriction can be removed by completing 30 quests and spending 10 hours in game. Doing the quests in all of your faction's starting zones will get you more than the 30 quests required. Joining a guild will also allow you to speak in guild chat.

Lunatic Guilds
There's a handful of guilds that will assist Lunatics in their goals:
<Level One Lunatic> is specifically designed for helping Lunatics. Their guild teleport is in booty Bay for easy access to Gurubashi Arena.
<Macrochelys> is helpful towards Lunatics and offers a high quality raiding scene should you choose to level up after finishing the challenge. Their guild teleport is to Azshara and comes with a gryphon to ride to Durotar.

There's also a few guilds with guild bases that don't tolerate Lunatics, so you'll have to get creative to get into them:
<The Scourge> - Tirisfal Glades
<The Scarlett Crusade> - Tirisfal Glades
<The Blackwing Guard> - Elwynn Forest (via Burning Steppes)
<The Lion's Pride Legion> - Elwynn Forest (via Duskwood)

The Setup
Mods used:
1. SuperWow
This mod is required to use ShaguScan, you'll also use it to launch wow.
2. VanillaTweaks
You'll use this mod to set your name plate view distance to 99.
3. ShaguScan
This mod allows you to make a list of available pvp targets near you. The scan parameters I use are(it should be copy-pastable for the mod filter line):
player,alliance,pvp,alive,attack
This makes it so that all living flagged alliance show up on a list, you'll change alliance to horde if you're playing an alliance. This should make hunting players less visually intensive.
4. ShaguPlates
Use this to customize nameplates so that health bars only show up for the unit you're targetting, and make the targetted hp bar easier to see. the options you're looking for are "Always Show On Target Units" and "Hide Healthbar On enemynpc/enemyplayer/neutralnpc" This way when you have nameplates on and you target a player on your ShaguScan list you're able to scan visually for them MUCH easier thanks to the VanillaTweaks nameplate distance increase.

Character:
Class:

Rogue - This is the class to pick for this challenge, they fit the bill in every way. Sinister Strike and Eviscerate provide ample damage on their own, plus they proc fiery. They scale VERY well on agility, even reaching above 100% dodge. The cherry on top is they have access to stealth at level 1.

Paladin – Can heal and tank well. Gear should be a mix of healing power, stamina, and armor. Weapon should be a Half-eaten Mutton Chop with fiery and +55 healing.
Cysthen's Paladin Guide

Warrior – Does good damage and can tank well. Gear should be enchanted with a lot of stamina and some strength. Weapons should have fiery, crusader, and lifesteal. Troll warriors can be scaled heavily with spirit to produce very high in combat regen.

Hunter – Does good damage, expensive to use because of twink ammo. Gear should be primarily agility, with some stamina. Weapons should have +25agi and fiery.

Shaman – Does good damage and some light tanking. Gear should be mostly stamina with some strength. Weapon should be a Half-eaten Mutton Chop with fiery.

Mage, Priest, Warlock, Druid – Able to do the challenge but are working entirely off stats instead of kit. Gear is entirely stamina. Weapon should be a Half-eaten Mutton Chop with fiery.

The tier order I believe I'd put the classes in is as follows: Rogue > Paladin > Warrior = Hunter > Shaman > Mage > Priest = Warlock = Druid

Race:
Goblin - Gives you +3 to dagger skill, and a 40% for 5s sprint on a 3min cd.
Night Elf - Gives you 1% increase to atk spd, casting spd, move spd, and dodge chance. You move 50% faster while dead, which is often. And you get access to shadowmeld which is an unmoving stealth on a 1min cd then doesn't break for 2 seconds after moving, or better stealth level if rogue. This race makes playing Warrior, Hunter, Priest, or Druid more viable then their non-NE counterparts.
Gnome - Gets 10 arcane resist which helps vs polymorph, and Escape Artist which removes and immobilization or movement speed reducing effect, on a 1.5min cd

Gear:
1. Helm
There's a few things you can get here like:
Woolen Cowl (lvl 6 ally quest reward)
Red Defias Mask (mob drop near deadmines)
Scruffy Cloth Hat (lvl 7 horde quest)
OR IF YOU BIG BALLIN'
Queen Azshara's Crown (Buy from Zeet Waxwrench in Sparkwater Port for 1k g) - 51 armor
Enchant - +8 Agi (Libram of Voracity, requires a lvl 50 to finish quest and apply the enchant)

2. Necklace
Voice Amplification Modulator (made by engineer)
Enchant - +6 Agi (Gemology Jewelcrafting 225)

3. Shoulders
Blackened Leather Spaulders (drops from Gregor Agamand) - BoP with 29 armor
Enchant - +16 stam and +100 armor
Gregor Agamand is a named mob located in northern Agamand Mills in northern Tirisfal Glades

4. Cape
Linen Cloak (made by a tailor) - 6 armor
Enchant - +3 Agi (Enchanting 225)

5. Chest
Dirty Leather Vest (Buy from starting zone leather vendor) - 33 armor
Enchant - +4 All Stats (Enchanting 300)

6. Wrist
Dirty Leather Bracers (Buy from starting zone leather vendor) - 15 armor
Enchant - +7 Agi (Enchanting 300)

7. Gloves
Dirty Leather Gloves (Buy from starting zone leather vendor) - 21 armor
Enchants - +15 Agi (Enchanting 300)

Enchant - +6 Agi (190 Blacksmithing)
"Squealer" Thornmantle can be found in a cave located near the quillboard chieftan's hut in Brambleblade Ravine located in southern Mulgore, within the starting zone

9. Legs
Dirty Leather Pants (Buy from starting zone leather vendor) - 29 armor
Enchant - +8 Agi (Libram of Voracity, requires a lvl 50 to finish quest and apply the enchant)

10. Boots

Enchant - Minor Speed (Enchanting 225)

11. Rings

Enchant - +6 Agi (Gemology Jewelcrafting 225)
You're going to want two of these rings

Arena Grand Master (Obtained from Gurubashi Arena chest quest) - 1% dodge, Use Effect: Absorbs 750 to 1250 damage and lasts 20 seconds

Scope - +7 dmg (Engineering 240)
Feathered Arrow (Quest reward from "Stolen Supplies" a Gelkis quest in Desolace) - 9.5 dmg

Minor Healing Potions - Use Effect: Restores 70 to 90 health

author: Cysthen
subject: Suggestion for Lunatic Gear Progression
content_md:
**Suggestion for Lunatic Gear Progression**

Not sure what the intentions are with Lunatic Gear moving forward with these Raids but we ran some tests on a vmangos server and believe Hit would be the perfect stat that speeds up our Runs without giving us too much power in PVP.

To the concern about PVP.  A Level 1 can already hit a Level 60 Player with very little miss chance. With that said Hit is weaker in PVP than Weapon Damage and there seems to be no issue giving us Weapon Damage.

I'd also like to note ****please stop having items be Grey or White you can't Master Loot them.****

 ****Notes:****
- We are aware Master Looter has been changed in 1.18.1 to affect Grey and White Rarity, it is currently bugged and forces Greys and Whites to be master looted while it's set to Uncommon.

- When it is fixed we'll change the current Weapons back to White Rarity. That said it doesn't change much else on this list as there isn't really anything that makes sense as White Rarity and the Hit items are appropriately Blue Rarity.

---
 **How PVE Hit Works**

Enemies have ****99% Avoidance from the front**** and that pretty much never changes.

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/3ZNrxAo.png)
---

Enemies have ****45-50% Miss chance from behind with 0 Hit**** and this value can change with Hit.

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/kapw1Rt.png)
---

 ****10% Hit**** on a vmangos Server makes it ****22-25% Miss chance from behind**** for reference.

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/hwxpoFm.png)
---

If we are going strictly off of the Test Results:
 ****44% from behind for Zero Hit.****
 ****22% from behind for 10%.****
That would put****each point of hit valued at 2.2% additional chance to hit from behind.****
Even with ****5% hit we would continue to miss exactly 33% of attacks****, according to these tests.

 ****We'd miss a third of attacks at 5%.****

You would still need 2 Rogues to Tank each target and how we play would remain the same, only slightly increase our overall clear times, as well as help Rogue Threat.

These tests were performed by Pyropal. Thank you.

---
 **How PVP Hit Works**

I've decided to add this section because there seems to be some reluctance from the developers to add hit items for us. I am not sure if the disconnect is a misunderstanding of how it works or just being unaware so I am clearing that up right now.

 2 Hours testing a Level 1 with 5 Weapon Skill hitting a Level 60 with 300 Defense:

[embed: https://www.youtube.com/embed/NUQEcrvCaOs]

---

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/vREFErv.jpeg)
---
We have 83% Hit/17% Miss against a Level 60.
The test results show that a Level 1 already has no issue hitting a majority of attacks on a player regardless of level.
These tests were done on a Level 60 in full Naxx Gear on Turtle WoW. With that proven it is our firm belief that Hit would very minimally affect PVP if that was a concern or reason for hesitation. Thank you.

---
 **Healing Threat Issues (Resolved)**  Saving the following for records. It appears they went with a Lunatic Exclusive option which is very impressive.
Thank you so much **Jamey**. Absolutely huge.

Currently ****Lesser Heal Rank 1, Healing Touch Rank 1, and Lesser Healing Wave Rank 1 all do twice as much threat**** as Paladin Heals. This is a major balance issue seeing as our content is heavily focused on managing threat. This causes a major bottleneck in performance for Priests, Druids, and Shamans when in reality they should have more healing over time potential than Paladins.

After researching this issue I've found that it can be addressed in two ways.

The easiest way is just running an SQL to reduce the threat of those 3 Rank 1 Healing Spell IDs. Seeing as Healing Threat isn't much of an issue endgame or outside of our content I see this as an extremely low risk solution.

 **SQL:** Code: Select all

```
REPLACE INTO `spell_threat` (`entry`, `Threat`, `multiplier`, `ap_bonus`) VALUES
(5185, 0, 0.5, 0),
(2050, 0, 0.5, 0),
(8004, 0, 0.5, 0);
```

The second more difficult solution is a C++ Core Edit that makes it so it only affects players with the Lunatic Spell ID. If this is to be considered I highly doubt this would be the method you all use compared to the above method. However I figured I'd include this to show how Lunatic Exclusive Changes could be made.

 **C++ Core Edit:** Code: Select all

```
// --- Configuration ---
// Level One Lunatic Challenge ID
#define SPELL_LEVEL_ONE_LUNATIC_ID 57736

// --- Implementation Logic ---
if (caster->HasAura(SPELL_LEVEL_ONE_LUNATIC_ID))
{
// Define targeted Rank 1 heal IDs
static const std::unordered_set<uint32> lowRankHealIds = {
 8004, // Lesser Healing Wave (Rank 1)
 5185, // Healing Touch (Rank 1)
 2050  // Lesser Heal (Rank 1)
};

// Retrieve the spell currently being processed
if (Spell* spell = caster->GetCurrentSpell(CURRENT_GENERIC_SPELL))
{
if (lowRankHealIds.find(spell->m_spellInfo->Id) != lowRankHealIds.end())
{
threat *= 0.5f; // Apply 50% threat reduction
}
}
}
```

Paladins were obviously given less healing threat due to the nature of how they have to run into melee range for Judgment. When you go into melee range the threat threshold is reduced by 20% making it much easier to take aggro. Priest, Druid, and Shaman Lunatics often run in to attack with Fishing Poles, or have enemies run past them that immediately aggro and kill them. As well as simply are unable to perform on the same level as Paladin due to this bottleneck even though they have more healing over time potential.

For these reasons it would be an extreme quality of life balance change for these spells to have the same threat output as Paladin. Thank you.

 ****Note to Developers:**** The original design of these items seemed to be a bit outdated.
For both 1-9 and 10-19 it didn't quite seem appropriate to create these with Class Restrictions as it would be practically the same items with additional Paladin and Shaman Versions (Lamellar, Lizardhide).

Doing Class Restrictions would also restrict certain classes (Druid, Shaman) from being able to use the Cloth Belt for Spell Damage. After deliberation with the community, this decision to exclude Class Restrictions was done on the premise that it would be less work and cover more bases at the same time.

Best in Slot would consist of items from every dungeon, Reputation Cape for Healers, Weapons, Belt for All Classes and Boots for PVP. This would make the challenge completely rounded.

 **10-19 Arathi Basin Reputation Rewards:**

content_html:
Suggestion for Lunatic Gear Progression

Not sure what the intentions are with Lunatic Gear moving forward with these Raids but we ran some tests on a vmangos server and believe Hit would be the perfect stat that speeds up our Runs without giving us too much power in PVP.

To the concern about PVP. A Level 1 can already hit a Level 60 Player with very little miss chance. With that said Hit is weaker in PVP than Weapon Damage and there seems to be no issue giving us Weapon Damage.

I'd also like to note please stop having items be Grey or White you can't Master Loot them.

Notes:
  • We are aware Master Looter has been changed in 1.18.1 to affect Grey and White Rarity, it is currently bugged and forces Greys and Whites to be master looted while it's set to Uncommon.
  • When it is fixed we'll change the current Weapons back to White Rarity. That said it doesn't change much else on this list as there isn't really anything that makes sense as White Rarity and the Hit items are appropriately Blue Rarity.

How PVE Hit Works

Enemies have 99% Avoidance from the front and that pretty much never changes.


Enemies have 45-50% Miss chance from behind with 0 Hit and this value can change with Hit.


10% Hit on a vmangos Server makes it 22-25% Miss chance from behind for reference.


If we are going strictly off of the Test Results:
44% from behind for Zero Hit.
22% from behind for 10%.

That would put each point of hit valued at 2.2% additional chance to hit from behind.

Even with 5% hit we would continue to miss exactly 33% of attacks, according to these tests.

We'd miss a third of attacks at 5%.

You would still need 2 Rogues to Tank each target and how we play would remain the same, only slightly increase our overall clear times, as well as help Rogue Threat.

These tests were performed by Pyropal. Thank you.

How PVP Hit Works

I've decided to add this section because there seems to be some reluctance from the developers to add hit items for us. I am not sure if the disconnect is a misunderstanding of how it works or just being unaware so I am clearing that up right now.

2 Hours testing a Level 1 with 5 Weapon Skill hitting a Level 60 with 300 Defense:

We have 83% Hit/17% Miss against a Level 60.
The test results show that a Level 1 already has no issue hitting a majority of attacks on a player regardless of level.
These tests were done on a Level 60 in full Naxx Gear on Turtle WoW. With that proven it is our firm belief that Hit would very minimally affect PVP if that was a concern or reason for hesitation. Thank you.

Healing Threat Issues (Resolved)
Saving the following for records. It appears they went with a Lunatic Exclusive option which is very impressive.
Thank you so much Jamey. Absolutely huge.

Currently Lesser Heal Rank 1, Healing Touch Rank 1, and Lesser Healing Wave Rank 1 all do twice as much threat as Paladin Heals. This is a major balance issue seeing as our content is heavily focused on managing threat. This causes a major bottleneck in performance for Priests, Druids, and Shamans when in reality they should have more healing over time potential than Paladins.

After researching this issue I've found that it can be addressed in two ways.

The easiest way is just running an SQL to reduce the threat of those 3 Rank 1 Healing Spell IDs. Seeing as Healing Threat isn't much of an issue endgame or outside of our content I see this as an extremely low risk solution.

SQL:

Code: Select all

REPLACE INTO `spell_threat` (`entry`, `Threat`, `multiplier`, `ap_bonus`) VALUES 
(5185, 0, 0.5, 0), 
(2050, 0, 0.5, 0), 
(8004, 0, 0.5, 0);

The second more difficult solution is a C++ Core Edit that makes it so it only affects players with the Lunatic Spell ID. If this is to be considered I highly doubt this would be the method you all use compared to the above method. However I figured I'd include this to show how Lunatic Exclusive Changes could be made.

C++ Core Edit:

Code: Select all

// --- Configuration ---
// Level One Lunatic Challenge ID
#define SPELL_LEVEL_ONE_LUNATIC_ID 57736 

// --- Implementation Logic ---
if (caster->HasAura(SPELL_LEVEL_ONE_LUNATIC_ID))
{
    // Define targeted Rank 1 heal IDs
    static const std::unordered_set<uint32> lowRankHealIds = {
        8004, // Lesser Healing Wave (Rank 1)
        5185, // Healing Touch (Rank 1)
        2050  // Lesser Heal (Rank 1)
    };

    // Retrieve the spell currently being processed
    if (Spell* spell = caster->GetCurrentSpell(CURRENT_GENERIC_SPELL))
    {
        if (lowRankHealIds.find(spell->m_spellInfo->Id) != lowRankHealIds.end())
        {
            threat *= 0.5f; // Apply 50% threat reduction
        }
    }
}
Paladins were obviously given less healing threat due to the nature of how they have to run into melee range for Judgment. When you go into melee range the threat threshold is reduced by 20% making it much easier to take aggro. Priest, Druid, and Shaman Lunatics often run in to attack with Fishing Poles, or have enemies run past them that immediately aggro and kill them. As well as simply are unable to perform on the same level as Paladin due to this bottleneck even though they have more healing over time potential.

For these reasons it would be an extreme quality of life balance change for these spells to have the same threat output as Paladin. Thank you.

Note to Developers

We are coding these items as a community, it takes a village and I personally have learned quite a lot in how much effort and time this takes. Hence the 1100+ thread edits and easily 50+ Hours we've put in. We are doing it in phases as we work down the forum thread.

All items are coded via a Spoiler under each item, including a picture of the model we choose.

However please note that obviously this won't include Entry ID's and whatever Flag ID is used for these to be Lunatic Exclusive. Those would have to be handled by you all of course unless we learn what our Flag ID is.

I would also like to add that aside from learning how to code some by making a template for reference, AI was NOT used AT ALL for any of these item names, flavor texts, model choices, or stat spreads. It was all done via conversation amongst the community with many people inputting what they think is best.

One last comment, we're new to a lot of this and New Spell IDs in particular are a lot more complicated it seems. We have included them however please feel free to double check those in particular.

Thank you all so much we are only trying to help.

Note to Developers: The original design of these items seemed to be a bit outdated.
For both 1-9 and 10-19 it didn't quite seem appropriate to create these with Class Restrictions as it would be practically the same items with additional Paladin and Shaman Versions (Lamellar, Lizardhide).

Doing Class Restrictions would also restrict certain classes (Druid, Shaman) from being able to use the Cloth Belt for Spell Damage. After deliberation with the community, this decision to exclude Class Restrictions was done on the premise that it would be less work and cover more bases at the same time.

Best in Slot would consist of items from every dungeon, Reputation Cape for Healers, Weapons, Belt for All Classes and Boots for PVP. This would make the challenge completely rounded.


10-19 Arathi Basin Reputation Rewards:
Including 10-19 to help facilitate Arathi Basin being added to both our brackets.

subject: Re: Suggestion for Lunatic Gear Progression
content_md:
> **Noephix wrote: Sun May 25, 2025 12:55 pm**
> Who told you lvl 1 lunatics are supposed to have gear progression?

I guess it would depend on your definition of "progression" wouldn't it? Based on the usual mmo term, it's safe to say that any new gear that provides better stats than your current gear would be considered progression. Some will argue that only getting new "tiers" of gear is progression and anything in between is meaningless.

If you're the kind of person to align with the first definition, then I'd say the two change logs that stated "new gear for lunatics in rfc and deadmines" seems like a reasonable place to assume we were informed from. So to answer your question the dev's/gm's would be the ones who said we have gear progression.

If you're more interested in the second definition then worry not. There isn't gear progression for lvl 1 lunatics and there likely won't be. Cysthen is requesting they add more "meaningless gear" for lvl 1s, so no need to concern yourself.

content_md:
> **berdal wrote: Tue Jan 27, 2026 11:17 am**
> This becomes too similar to lvl60 endgame IMHO.
>
>  I'd say tone it down a little. Items are too powerful. Most items should have at most one stat modifier, and be white/green/blue, instead of green/blue/epic. Also decrease drop rate.
>
>  But agree, L1L needs item proper rebalance on existing items, drops from all/more bosses.
>
>  But LOVE your enthusiasm! Keep at it :) I hope you get their attention.

I only made the Chest pieces that way, and the Cape and Chest is already 25% Droprate.

White Items can't be Master Looted even if the Loot Rules are set to Common. On Master Loot right clicking a White Item even with those Loot Rules Set just loots the item. We've had many mishaps and accidental loots with new Raid Leaders due to this issue. That's why I made the move to Green/Blue/Epic instead. And the only Epics are on Mutanus, Arugal, and Gnomeregan which is entirely appropriate having personally done Mutanus.

I tried to walk a fine line on item power for this to be as digestible for the Devs as possible. It's hard to understand until you see it but Hit isn't as strong as people think it is. 1% makes you go from 50% Miss from behind to 47% Miss. You aren't going to feel that change at all as a player until you get more.

For example we used Fire-toasted Bun (2% Hit, Limited Use) from Fire Festival and could hardly even tell if the 2% Hit did anything. I know it did, but when you're still missing 44% of attacks it's hard to tell.

It's not going to drastically change how we play, I stopped at 5% Hit on here because I think it's an appropriate stopping point. It limits us to missing a third of attacks instead of half. Not to mention it requires us to drop 12 Stamina not using Fishing Boots and to buy another Sapphiron Enchant to benefit from the full 5%. So there's quite a lot of trade offs happening and helping fund endgame 60 Guilds. On top of earning the items in the first place.

I think it should look similar to 60 endgame. It's already its own form of endgame. The only difference being our items are silly and all have flavor texts using the existing items for example.

I gave the Kresh Shield 3 Stamina to be a Furbolg Pouch Equivalent for Shield Users with 7 Stamina Enchant.

What's on display here, would create a fully fleshed out alternative endgame to the existing one at Level 60. Available to all players meanwhile being extremely accessible to casuals/newcomers, since all you have to do is log in on a newly created Level 1. As well as help the economy with the repeated need for enchants and a significant gold dump required for the Gnomeregan pieces.

Some of the later pieces might get reevaluated as I get to coding them. For example 1% Meditation wasn't an available Spell ID so I changed the Healing Mace in Wailing Caverns to 2 Healing instead of 4.

As for future items with 2% Health Regeneration in Combat for example, the current lowest available Spell ID is 5% so I'll have to create a new Spell ID for that as it's not ideal to settle for Health per 5 with Troll Warrior.

content_html:
Update: 2/11/26 (Resolved) Thank you Jamey
Edited to address our Priest, Druid, and Shaman Healers who are bottlenecked with threat issues compared to Paladin for a very stupid reason. I've added the following section to address this problem.
Healing Threat Issues

Currently Lesser Heal Rank 1, Healing Touch Rank 1, and Lesser Healing Wave Rank 1 all do twice as much threat as Paladin Heals. This is a major balance issue seeing as our content is heavily focused on managing threat. This causes a major bottleneck in performance for Priests, Druids, and Shamans when in reality they should have more healing over time potential than Paladins.

After researching this issue I've found that it can be addressed in two ways.

Note to Developers: I haven't had a chance to test these yet on a vmangos server however I am looking into it and will try to include proof of these solutions working in the future.

The easiest way is just running an SQL to reduce the threat of those 3 Rank 1 Healing Spell IDs. Seeing as Healing Threat isn't much of an issue endgame or outside of our content I see this as an extremely low risk solution.

SQL:

Code: Select all

REPLACE INTO `spell_threat` (`entry`, `Threat`, `multiplier`, `ap_bonus`) VALUES 
(5185, 0, 0.5, 0), 
(2050, 0, 0.5, 0), 
(8004, 0, 0.5, 0);

The second more difficult solution is a C++ Core Edit that makes it so it only affects players with the Lunatic Spell ID. If this is to be considered I highly doubt this would be the method you all use compared to the above method. However I figured I'd include this to show how Lunatic Exclusive Changes could be made.

C++ Core Edit:

Code: Select all

// --- Configuration ---
// Level One Lunatic Challenge ID
#define SPELL_LEVEL_ONE_LUNATIC_ID 57736 

// --- Implementation Logic ---
if (caster->HasAura(SPELL_LEVEL_ONE_LUNATIC_ID))
{
    // Define targeted Rank 1 heal IDs
    static const std::unordered_set<uint32> lowRankHealIds = {
        8004, // Lesser Healing Wave (Rank 1)
        5185, // Healing Touch (Rank 1)
        2050  // Lesser Heal (Rank 1)
    };

    // Retrieve the spell currently being processed
    if (Spell* spell = caster->GetCurrentSpell(CURRENT_GENERIC_SPELL))
    {
        if (lowRankHealIds.find(spell->m_spellInfo->Id) != lowRankHealIds.end())
        {
            threat *= 0.5f; // Apply 50% threat reduction
        }
    }
}
Paladins were obviously given less healing threat due to the nature of how they have to run into melee range for Judgment. When you go into melee range the threat threshold is reduced by 20% making it much easier to take aggro. Priest, Druid, and Shaman Lunatics often run in to attack with Fishing Poles, or have enemies run past them that immediately aggro and kill them. As well as simply are unable to perform on the same level as Paladin due to this bottleneck even though they have more healing over time potential.

For these reasons it would be an extreme quality of life balance change for these spells to have the same threat output as Paladin. Thank you.

Emote ID: **133**
Triggers: **Menu 1**
Shows Text:

Greetings... Uhm could you move a bit to the left my device is losing signal... Thank you that's much better.

If you happen upon anything of value and are in need of help let me know I'm very good with my hands.

Choice: **What are you doing up here?**

Emote ID: **5**
Shows Text:

Honestly the signal downstairs is horrible! I have many clients I am in contact with and they are in need of my expertise.

I took this job because I heard it's just guarding a post but they have everything under control! It's great I can contact my clients at the same time and besides I could really use the funds.

Choice: **You're low on gold. Did something happen?**

Redirects to **Menu 3**
Emote ID: **1**
Shows Text:

Let's just say I had a handful of deals go bad. I did everything like they wanted but they didn't like the outcome. However the issue really is that I needed some materials for projects and told them I'd get their gold as soon as I finished those jobs.

I've learned that you can't always trust people to pay out and I'm in a bit of a bad spot right now. However I have a few projects in the works and I'm confident I'll pull through.

Choice: **What did you mean if I find anything of value you'd be able to help?**

Redirects to **Menu 4**
Emote ID: **133**
Shows Text:

Well I've been known to make nothing into something, there's a lot of junk scattered around Gnomeregan and I'm sure if I could get my hands on some of it I might be able to make wonders.

However like I said I'm on hard times right now, if you find something you think is interesting bring it to me and we'll see if I get inspired.

This was an immense amount of effort, what the developers do on this server is an insurmountable feat and we have the utmost respect for what they do. Moreso after having done this.

Notes:
  • Most importantly he's holding a Remote type of item. Item ID: 60539 is perfect. https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60539
  • We like Display ID: 6628 overall however he could have Display ID: 20341's outfit to differentiate him, keeping the goggles obviously.

NPC Greeting:

Emote ID: 133
Triggers: Menu 1
Shows Text:

Greetings... Uhm could you move a bit to the left my device is losing signal... Thank you that's much better.

If you happen upon anything of value and are in need of help let me know I'm very good with my hands.

Choice: What are you doing up here?

Redirects to Menu 2
Emote ID: 5
Shows Text:

Honestly the signal downstairs is horrible! I have many clients I am in contact with and they are in need of my expertise.

I took this job because I heard it's just guarding a post but they have everything under control! It's great I can contact my clients at the same time and besides I could really use the funds.

Choice: You're low on gold. Did something happen?

Redirects to Menu 3
Emote ID: 1
Shows Text:

Let's just say I had a handful of deals go bad. I did everything like they wanted but they didn't like the outcome. However the issue really is that I needed some materials for projects and told them I'd get their gold as soon as I finished those jobs.

I've learned that you can't always trust people to pay out and I'm in a bit of a bad spot right now. However I have a few projects in the works and I'm confident I'll pull through.

Choice: What did you mean if I find anything of value you'd be able to help?

Redirects to Menu 4
Emote ID: 133
Shows Text:

Well I've been known to make nothing into something, there's a lot of junk scattered around Gnomeregan and I'm sure if I could get my hands on some of it I might be able to make wonders.

However like I said I'm on hard times right now, if you find something you think is interesting bring it to me and we'll see if I get inspired.

• Dodge Chance: ~0.91% per Agility
• Critical Strike Chance: ~0.455% per Agility

![:sparkles:](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/2728.svg) Final Tips

• Eviscerate is bait — Missing hits wastes energy, Sinister strike only costs 4 Energy if it doesn't hit.

• Fiery vs +15 Agility in PvP — If you cant consistently hit someone higher level, you're better off using +15 Agility

• Patience is key — Timbermaw rep and Arena Grindmaster suck.

• Positioning is Important — You're only melee immune from the front. You cant dodge while "casting" so no *"bubble hearths"* and be wary using range.

• Fiery in PvE — 100% Not worth it, Only procs off hits and isn't guaranteed you're better off with higher crit chance.

• Fiery Crits — Fiery can crit if you have 10% base spell crit from Rallying Cry of the Dragonslayer. DM Int cape, gives .06% Spell crit (meme).

• BiS: Goblin Rocket Boots (41) \*³ — Engineering *(Use: Increase your run speed by 70% for 20 sec. (5m CD)*
• Dirty / Cracked Leather (23)

Rings
• Silver Piffeny Ring — Qixdi (Booty Bay)
• Broken Stonemason's Signet (Vanity Item) — VanCleef (DM)

Trinkets
• Insignia of the Horde / Alliance
• Arena Grand Master (1% Dodge, Absorbs 750 to 1250 damage, Lasts 20s. 30m CD) — Turn in 12 Arena Trinkets (STV)
• Cinder Bracers (Summons Cinder Elemental 1-3 dps) \*⁴
• Fox's Spirit Stone (Summons Spirit Fox 1-3 dps) \*⁵

Main-hand Weapon
• BiS: The Blazing Pan (5–8 Dmg, Speed 2.00) — Oggleflint (RFC)
• Simple Dagger (3–6 Dmg, Speed 1.80) — Auction House

Ranged
• Cadet's Bow + Rough (+1.5 DPS) / Feathered Arrow (+9.5 DPS) \*⁶
• Small Throwing Knife (+1.3 DPS) \*⁷
• Crude Throwing Axe (+1.3 DPS) \*⁷

Offhand
• Furbolg Medicine Pouch (+10 Stam, 100 HP every 1s for 10s, 30m CD) — Timbermaw Rep (Honored)

Notes
*¹ icon represents Armor value.
*² Dirty (Horde) vs Cracked (Alliance) is cosmetic only — vendor gear.
*³ Rocket Boots have BiS Armor but destroy themselves on use & may kill you. Bring spares.
*⁴ Only available during Midsummer Fire Festival.
*⁵ Technically a toy now — rare drop from Spirit Fox in Winterspring.
*⁶ Arrows are BiS but very expensive.
*⁷ Throwing weapons avoid cast time — better for PvP kiting.

---

Enchants
"Armor? Avoidance?"
"NANO ENCHANTS, SON."

I’ve got Fiery Weapon and Furbolg Medicine Pouch,
+88 Agility stitched into every thread,
and Rocket Boots that explode if I blink wrong.

"You think a level 60 scares me? I’ve dodged god."

Weapon
• Fiery Weapon — PvP
• +15 Agility — PvE/PvP

Head
• +8 Agility — PvE \*¹
• +100 Hitpoints — Lesser Arcanum of Constitution \*²

Shoulders
• +16 Stamina / 100 Armor — Fortitude of the Scourge \*³

Cloak
• +3 Agility

Chest
• +4 Stats — BiS \*⁴
• +3 Stats — Budget alternative

Gloves
• +15 Agility

Bracers
• +7 Agility

:briefs: Belt
• +6 Agility

Legs
• +8 Agility — PvE
• +100 Hitpoints — Lesser Arcanum of Constitution

:hiking_boot: Boots
• +8% Minor Speed — PvP \*⁷
• +7 Agility — PvE
• +15 Stamina — Defensive

Necklace & Rings
• +6 Agility

Ranged (Bow)
• +7 Damage — Sniper Scope

Notes
\*¹ Full Agility enchants are necessary for all races to hit 100% Dodge in PvE.
\*² The only exception is Night Elves & Gnomes, who can take +100 HP in one slot.
\*³ Fortitude of the Scourge costs 300–400g.
\*⁴ +4 Stats is significantly more expensive than +3 Stats.
\*⁵ Total Agility is +87 with +3 Stats, and +88 with +4 Stats.
\*⁶ Carry two weapons: one for PvP (Fiery), one for PvE (+15 Agi).
\*⁷ Bring two boots: one with Agility for PvE, one with Speed for PvP.

---

Final Tips

• Eviscerate is bait — Missing hits wastes energy, Sinister strike only costs 4 Energy if it doesn't hit.

• Fiery vs +15 Agility in PvP — If you cant consistently hit someone higher level, you're better off using +15 Agility

• Patience is key — Timbermaw rep and Arena Grindmaster suck.

• Positioning is Important — You're only melee immune from the front. You cant dodge while "casting" so no *"bubble hearths"* and be wary using range.

• Fiery in PvE — 100% Not worth it, Only procs off hits and isn't guaranteed you're better off with higher crit chance.

• Fiery Crits — Fiery can crit if you have 10% base spell crit from Rallying Cry of the Dragonslayer. DM Int cape, gives .06% Spell crit (meme).

• How to dodge kite backwards — <https://youtu.be/oJc53OOgmzo>

• Getting to Durotar as a Gigalliance — <https://youtu.be/5JKwWJPu3N4>

author: StabsMcKenzy
subject: Re: Rogue Guide
content_md:
I like all the cute little emotes. To answer your questions though:

Goblin Rocket Boots: What does "explode" mean? Does it just mean loss of all durability (repairable) or do you mean they actually disappear and you'd have to acquire new ones?

They actually disappear and leave behind so scrap parts and a pair of black mageweave boots. However, if you have extra pairs of goblin rocket boots in your inventory those will break first before your equip ones. so if your equip ones have movement speed enchanted on them and none of the boots in your inventory do then you've got a way to safeguard the enchanted boots, keep in mind that as long as you have the speed buff from the boots the extra pairs can still break. Basically as long as the buff speed buff is active every second you have a chance of your boots exploding, so in the worst possible case you could use 20 pairs of boots over the course of the 20 second speed boost.

Silver Piffeny Ring: The goblin in mention sells a variety of rings which are wearable by level 1s in the price range of 1-250 gold. Is it correct to assume that any of these rings are viable (even the ones costing 1 gold)?

Nope, only the ones that cost 10g or more are enchantable.

Simple Dagger: You said it youself that missed swings means reducred Fiery proc. Could it be that the Rusted Pirate Dagger (2-4 dmg, 1.6 atk spd) or Skinning Knife (2-5 dmg, 1.6 atk spd) is the better option for the fiery enchantment due to the increased attack speed? Has anyone compared the dps?

Simple Dagger and Keen Machete are essentially equal in dps, not accounting for weapon skill racials. The only better weapon then those 2 is the Blazing Pan from RFC. Rusted Pirae Dagger and Skinning Knife are both worse.

Hope this helps, if you ever have questions feel free to reach out via the lunatic discord.
